questions.subject: Geography
questions.question:
Consider the following about the Pacific Ring of Fire:
1. It is a horseshoe-shaped zone of frequent earthquakes and volcanic eruptions
2. It is associated with convergent plate boundaries (subduction zones)
3. Mount Fuji (Japan), Mount St. Helens (USA), and Mount Pinatubo (Philippines) are on it
4. India lies entirely within the Ring of Fire
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 3 correct. Statement 4 WRONG — India does NOT lie in the Ring of Fire. India is on the Indo-Australian Plate, far from the Pacific Ring. India's earthquakes are from continental collision (India-Eurasia) not subduction. Ring of Fire: 40,000 km arc around Pacific — from New Zealand → Indonesia → Philippines → Japan → Aleutians → Western Americas. ~75% of world's active volcanoes and ~90% of earthquakes occur here.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question:
With reference to types of volcanic eruptions:
1. Shield volcanoes (like Hawaii) have gentle slopes and fluid basaltic lava
2. Stratovolcanoes (composite) are tall, steep, and explosively dangerous
3. Calderas form when a volcano collapses into its emptied magma chamber
4. All volcanic eruptions produce the same type of lava
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 3 correct. Statement 4 WRONG — lava types differ significantly. Basaltic lava (low silica, low viscosity, fluid — shield volcanoes like Hawaii). Andesitic lava (intermediate — stratovolcanoes). Rhyolitic lava (high silica, very viscous, explosive — Yellowstone type). Lava type determines eruption style: fluid basalt = effusive (rivers of lava); viscous rhyolite = explosive (pyroclastic flows, ash clouds). This is why some volcanoes are deadly (Vesuvius) and others are tourist attractions (Hawaii).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question:
Consider the following recently active/notable volcanoes:
1. Mount Etna (Italy) - Europe's most active volcano
2. Kilauea (Hawaii) - one of the world's most active shield volcanoes
3. Eyjafjallajökull (Iceland) - 2010 eruption disrupted European aviation
4. Krakatoa (Indonesia) - located between Java and Sumatra
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: All correct. Etna (Sicily, Italy): Europe's tallest and most active volcano (~3,357m), erupts frequently. Kilauea (Hawaii): shield volcano, continuous eruption for decades, creates new land. Eyjafjallajökull (April 2010): ash cloud grounded 100,000+ flights across Europe for days — exposed aviation vulnerability to volcanic events. Krakatoa/Krakatau (Sunda Strait, between Java and Sumatra): catastrophic 1883 eruption; Anak Krakatau ('Child of Krakatoa') formed in 1927, erupted again 2018 causing tsunami.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question:
With reference to India's volcanic history and features:
1. Barren Island (Andaman) is India's only confirmed active volcano
2. The Deccan Traps are remnants of massive volcanic eruptions 66 million years ago
3. Deccan Trap eruptions may have contributed to dinosaur extinction
4. Dhinodhar Hills (Gujarat) are volcanic in origin
questions.explanation: All correct. Barren Island: last erupted 2020, only active volcano in South Asia (135 km NE of Port Blair). Deccan Traps: basaltic lava covering 500,000 sq km (Maharashtra, MP, Gujarat, Karnataka) — one of largest volcanic provinces globally. Erupted over ~30,000 years around K-Pg boundary (66 Ma). 'Volcanic Winter' theory: massive CO2/SO2 release contributed to mass extinction (alongside Chicxulub asteroid). Dhinodhar Hills (Kutch, Gujarat): volcanic plug, ~500m height, tertiary volcanic activity evidence.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question:
Consider the following about plate tectonics and India:
1. India separated from Gondwanaland approximately 140 million years ago
2. The Indian Plate is moving northward at approximately 5 cm per year
3. The collision of Indian and Eurasian plates created the Himalayas
4. The Indian Plate is entirely continental with no oceanic crust
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 3 correct. Statement 4 WRONG — the Indian Plate includes BOTH continental and oceanic crust. The oceanic part lies under the Indian Ocean (south of the subcontinent). The continental part is the Indian landmass. India separated from Madagascar ~88 Ma and from Antarctica/Australia earlier. Drift rate ~5 cm/year (one of the fastest). Collision began ~50 Ma — Himalayas are still rising (1-2 cm/year). Earthquakes in the Himalayan region result from this ongoing collision.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question:
With reference to hotspot volcanism:
1. Hotspot volcanoes form over mantle plumes unrelated to plate boundaries
2. Hawaii is the classic example of hotspot volcanism
3. As a plate moves over a hotspot, it creates a chain of volcanic islands
4. The Deccan Traps were formed by the Reunion hotspot
questions.explanation: All correct. Hotspots: stationary mantle plumes of abnormally hot material rising from deep mantle. Unlike plate boundary volcanism, hotspots are intra-plate. Hawaii: Pacific Plate moves over Hawaiian hotspot → chain of islands (oldest island = Kauai, youngest = Big Island/active). Deccan Traps: formed when Indian Plate passed over the Reunion hotspot (now under Reunion Island in Indian Ocean, 5,000 km away — proving India moved north). Yellowstone (USA) is another hotspot example.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question:
Consider the following about tsunamis:
1. They are caused by underwater earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, or landslides
2. The 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami was triggered by a magnitude 9.1 earthquake off Sumatra
3. Tsunami speed in deep ocean can exceed 700-800 km/h
4. India's tsunami early warning centre is located in Chennai
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 3 correct. Statement 4 WRONG — India's Tsunami Early Warning Centre (ITEWC) is at INCOIS (Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services) in HYDERABAD, not Chennai. Established after the devastating 2004 tsunami (230,000+ deaths, including 10,000+ in India). The centre uses seismometers, tide gauges, DART buoys, and satellite data. Can issue warnings within 10-20 minutes of an earthquake. 2004 tsunami: epicentre off Banda Aceh, Sumatra (9.1 magnitude, 3rd largest ever recorded).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question:
With reference to the East African Rift System:
1. It is an example of a divergent plate boundary on a continent
2. Africa is slowly splitting into the Nubian (western) and Somali (eastern) plates
3. The Great Rift Valley lakes (Tanganyika, Malawi) formed due to this rifting
4. In millions of years, eastern Africa will separate to form a new ocean
questions.explanation: All correct. East African Rift: world's largest active continental rift system (~3,500 km from Afar Triple Junction to Mozambique). Divergent boundary: Nubian Plate (west) separating from Somali Plate (east) at ~2.5 mm/year. Rift valley lakes formed in downdropped grabens (Tanganyika = 2nd deepest lake globally). Active volcanism: Kilimanjaro, Nyiragongo (DRC), Ol Doinyo Lengai (Tanzania). In ~10 million years: new ocean (like Red Sea, which formed similarly from Afro-Arabian rift).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question:
Consider the following about earthquake measurement:
1. Richter Scale is logarithmic — each whole number = 10x amplitude increase
2. Moment Magnitude Scale (Mw) has replaced Richter for large earthquakes
3. Modified Mercalli Intensity (MMI) measures the effects/damage of earthquakes
4. P-waves arrive before S-waves because they travel through both solids and liquids
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: All correct. Richter (1935): logarithmic (Mag 7 = 10x amplitude of Mag 6, but ~31.6x MORE energy). Moment Magnitude: preferred for large quakes (>7) as Richter saturates. MMI (I to XII): damage-based (I = not felt; XII = total destruction) — varies by distance, soil type, building construction. P-waves (Primary/Push): fastest, compressional, travel through all media (solid/liquid/gas). S-waves (Secondary/Shear): slower, transverse, travel only through solids (cannot pass through liquid outer core — this is how we know outer core is liquid!).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question:
With reference to volcanic ash and its global impact:
1. Large eruptions can inject sulphur dioxide into the stratosphere
2. This creates aerosol particles that reflect sunlight, causing temporary cooling
3. The 1991 Mount Pinatubo eruption cooled global temperatures by ~0.5°C
4. Volcanic winter has no documented historical precedent
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 3 correct. Statement 4 WRONG — volcanic winter HAS documented precedents. Most famous: 1815 Mount Tambora (Indonesia) eruption → 'Year Without a Summer' (1816) — global crop failures, famines in Europe/North America. Also: 1783 Laki (Iceland) eruption caused European famine. ~74,000 years ago: Toba super-eruption (Sumatra) may have caused a 6-10 year volcanic winter, possibly reducing human population to ~10,000 ('genetic bottleneck' theory). Pinatubo (1991): 0.5°C cooling for 2 years, depleted ozone layer.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question:
Consider the following about India's seismic zonation:
1. India is divided into 4 seismic zones (II, III, IV, V) by BIS
2. Zone V (very high risk) includes: entire NE India, J&K, Uttarakhand, parts of HP
3. Delhi falls in Zone IV (high risk)
4. No major city in peninsular India falls in Zone III or above
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 3 correct. Statement 4 WRONG — several peninsular cities ARE in Zone III or above. Mumbai (Zone III), Pune (Zone III), Bangalore (Zone II-III boundary), Ahmedabad (Zone III — devastated in 2001 Bhuj quake which was Zone V). Peninsular India is NOT completely safe. Zone I was removed in 2002 revision (entire India is now minimum Zone II). Key: seismic risk depends on: zone, soil type (amplification), building codes compliance. Even 'moderate' Zone III can be deadly if buildings aren't earthquake-resistant.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question:
With reference to submarine volcanoes and volcanic islands:
1. Iceland is located on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge (divergent boundary)
2. Indonesia has the most active volcanoes of any country
3. The Mariana Trench is associated with a subduction zone
4. Volcanic islands like Hawaii eventually sink and become seamounts/atolls
questions.explanation: All correct. Iceland: sits ON the Mid-Atlantic Ridge where North American and Eurasian plates diverge — unique place where mid-ocean ridge is above sea level. Indonesia: 130+ active volcanoes (most globally) due to multiple subduction zones (Pacific, Philippine, Indo-Australian plates converging). Mariana Trench (~11 km deep): Pacific Plate subducting under Philippine Plate. Hawaiian chain: as plate moves away from hotspot, islands subside (thermal contraction) → become flat-topped seamounts (guyots) → if coral grows, become atolls (Darwin's theory of atoll formation).
